videos.t: Ever Blooming Mechanical Tulip WiFi upgrade
videos.desc:
So I've just upgraded my Ever Blooming Mechanical Tulip with ESP32 WiFi microcontroller. So now I can control it remotely. Which is so great!

https://jiripraus.cz/

https://www.instructables.com/id/Ever-Blooming-Mechanical-Tulip/
This is my free-form build of Arduino UNO. It has no circuit board and the same features as the Arduino UNO development board. Here it is blinking for the first time.

I build sculptures out of brass wires and since I hate repeating creating same part over and over again I decided to build a wire bending CNC machine that would do the job for me. So far it is still an early prototype but looks promising! The goal is to build a machine that has most of the parts 3D printer or easy to get so everybody can build it at home.

https://hackaday.io/project/166369-wire-bender
https://twitter.com/jipraus
https://www.instagram.com/jiripraus/
The first successful bend with my 3D printed wire bending machine. A lot of scrapped wire was made in the process. Still, the biggest problem is insufficient adhesion of drive gears.

I combined my passion for free-form art circuits and engineering. This is my wire bender machine that can bend quite precise shapes. I've used it to create a simple hex LED jewelry badge. Enjoy.

https://hackaday.io/project/166369-wire-bender
https://jiripraus.cz
https://twitter.com/jipraus
https://www.instagram.com/jiripraus/

Yes, it can make springs. Totally satisfying to watch. Enjoy!

https://hackaday.io/project/166369-wi...
https://jiripraus.cz
https://twitter.com/jipraus
https://www.instagram.com/jiripraus/

Build a wire bending machine capable of bending 0.8/0.9/1 mm wire into any 2D shape. The coolest thing I was able to make with it so far was the spring. How cool is that?

The main goal was to make it quite precise. Other DIY wire bending machines are not very precise and their bends tend to have quite a big radius. I like to work with nice sharp bends!

The second goal was to make it as easy to build as possible with commonly available parts and components. All the structural parts are 3D printed and all the metal parts are available in most of the hardware stores.

Heart out of 46 NeoPixels. Full video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=keD2IxvzPSs

I am back again with my brass wires and soldering iron. This time I built an LED heart badge that features an array of programmable LEDs. LEDs are controlled with tiny ATTiny85 embedded on the back. The whole sculpture is very compact and easy to wear.

Used components
- 3D printed template (http://jiripraus.cz/downloads/neoheart.stl)
- 0.8mm brass wire
- WS2812b RGB LEDs
- ATTiny85 microcontroller
- 1000mAh LiPo battery
- 5V Micro USB 1A 18650 Lithium Battery Charging Board
- 0.3mm insulated copper wire
- small switch

Code
https://gist.github.com/jpraus/07995fcb9248f39292aa7d68cc030bf6

🎉 Today it is exactly 1 year since my first-ever free-form sculpture - the Arduino Nano based snowflake. It's been quite a ride since then.

I took it out of the shelf and gave the old lady some nice treatments. Hot IPA bath, hot-air drying, and juicy USB power. It shines like a year ago. Family reunion with the other flakes.

videos.t: LED sphere with 194 LEDs and how to build it
videos.desc:
Everybody is crazy about LED cubes. I wanted to create one myself, but I wanted to make it an even bigger challenge and since I am not limited by the use of circuit boards and can make it free-form. I've decided to make an LED ball. I believe this is the first instance of air-wire LED ball in the world.

It's controlled by ESP32 board and powered by 1000mAh LiPo battery. So not only it is wearable but also can be controlled via mobile phone.

This video is sponsored by https://www.samepage.io.

Used components:
- WS2818b LEDs
- TTGO v1.7 ESP32 board
- 1000mAh LiPo battery
- 0.8mm brass-wire

videos.t: Artist's tribute to legendary GameBoy Color
videos.desc:
Handmade Brass GameBoy Color. A free-form tribute to legendary GameBoy Color I played when I was a kid. I am creating an emulator version based on Odroid GO emulator firmware running ESP-32. I gave it my artistic style - it's made from brass.

All models and techniques are available on my https://www.patreon.com/jiripraus page to download. If you want to ask me anything or get assistance, join Maker tier and I will be at your service!

This video is sponsored by https://www.samepage.io.

Based on firmware by https://www.hardkernel.com/shop/odroid-go/

Build! Don't forget to share your creation
